title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 11
paragraphs: So Pausanias with his army had gone out of Sparta. The envoys, at daybreak, knowing nothing of this departure, came before the Ephors intending to leave themselves, each for his own city; and when they had come before them, they said this: “You, Lacedaemonians, are staying here celebrating the Hyakinthia and amusing yourselves, while you have left your allies to destruction. And the Athenians, being wronged by you and lacking allies, will make peace with the Persians on whatever terms they can. Once they have made peace, we clearly become allies of the king and therefore we shall join him in expeditions against whatever land the Persians lead us; and then you shall learn what the outcome of this matter will be for you.” When the envoys said this, the Ephors replied, swearing it with an oath, that they supposed by now the men were at Orestheion, on their way against the strangers — for they used to call the barbarians “strangers.” So the envoys, knowing nothing of this, asked what the words meant, and asking they learned the whole truth. Struck with amazement, they set out in pursuit as quickly as possible; and along with them five thousand picked Lacedaemonian hoplites of the perioikoi did the same.
